newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa rejects open slot trading plans.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa rejects open slot trading plans.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa is not interested in an open airport slot trading system, chairman Juergen Weber said.
The existing "pragmatic" system worked and should be retained since new rules could not please everyone, he told the 5th Frankfurt Air Travel Symposium at Frankfurt airport.
"The subject of slot trading is dangerous because it can be abused and I see a certain danger," he said in reply to questions from airline and airport managers.
New entrants should be given the chance to open new routes but not at the cost of established carriers, he added.
"I see a slot like a factory. When you build a factory, you have start-up costs and it loses money sometimes until it really works and then makes money."
If after that investment a slot is taken away and given to a new airline on that route," that cannot be right," he added.
Lufthansa had not previously indicated its stance on the current debate over how to reform airport slot allocation, industry observers said.
